citations.title: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities
citations.requirement: Lists 18 personal rights: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation or abuse; being told how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman; leaving at any time and not being locked in; private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care; moving out. Subsection (b) bars denial of admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, and association, based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive the (b) protections.

citations.title: Emergency Disaster Plan
citations.requirement: A written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan. It must cover: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notifying a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements-General
citations.requirement: Personnel must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need. Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. Staff assisting with personal ADLs get initial and annual training under HSC §§1569.625 and 1569.69, plus first aid from a qualified provider. Required training topics are listed, with trainer qualifications and documentation in personnel records. All personnel need a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan.

citations.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services
citations.requirement: Requires a plan for incidental medical and dental care. Staff may only assist with self-administered medications and may not give injections unless authorized by law. Assistance cannot include forcing, hiding or camouflaging medications. PRN rules: a signed, dated physician order on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours. Central storage in a locked place, in the original container, with a record kept at least 1 year. Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, with a record kept at least 3 years. First aid kit; emergency numbers posted; ambulance number available; call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health.

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Individual written agreement in 12-point type, plain language, with titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Copy given immediately, and a copy or notice of availability posted. Must specify basic services, additional services, rates, payment, 60 days' written notice of rate changes, refund conditions, preadmission fee limits and refunds, visiting policy, firearms policy, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman. LIC 9158 is required when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

citations.title: Prohibited Health Conditions
citations.requirement: Residents who need health services for, or have, these conditions cannot be admitted or retained: stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, and tracheostomies. The list is not exhaustive ("including, but not limited to").

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: (a)(1) Written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse). (a)(2) Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer. (a)(3) Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority, and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency. (b),(c) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours. (d),(e),(f) Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice; notice to applicants before signing; civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. (g) Notice of a new administrator within 30 days. (h) Change of chief corporate officer within 15 working days.

citations.title: Night Supervision (RCFE)
citations.requirement: Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight. 16–100 residents: one employee awake on duty plus one on call within 10 minutes. Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained. (Per fact-checked research S7.)

citations.title: Care of Persons with Dementia
citations.requirement: In homes with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation. (Per fact-checked research S8.)

citations.title: Advertising Dementia Special Care
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises dementia care must have a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep advertisements for 3 years. (Per fact-checked research S27 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan. (Per fact-checked research S23.)

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Fire clearance is required before licensure. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. (Per fact-checked research S28.)

citations.title: Personal Accommodations and Services
citations.requirement: No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family. (Per fact-checked research S24.)

citations.title: Maintenance and Operation
citations.requirement: Heat of at least 68°F; hot water 105–120°F; plant maintenance standards; private water supply testing (annually for capacity 7–15). (Per fact-checked research S69 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and staff before they work or are present. (Per fact-checked research S29.)

citations.title: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables
citations.requirement: If the facility holds resident cash, it must keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as the residents' money, with no commingling. LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond. (Per fact-checked research S70.)

citations.title: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character, and must be certified. Added education and experience for 16+ beds. Must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent. (Per fact-checked research S14.)

citations.title: Infection Control Requirements
citations.requirement: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282). Name an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional. Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request. (Per fact-checked research S32.)

citations.title: Hospice Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request. (Per fact-checked research S26.)

citations.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal
citations.requirement: Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination against admission criteria before admission. (Per fact-checked research S35 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Administrator certification
citations.requirement: 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days. 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. (Per fact-checked research S13.)

citations.title: Direct care staff training
citations.requirement: 40 hours initial: 20 before working alone and 20 within 4 weeks. The first 20 include 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. 20 hours annually, including 8 hours dementia. (Per fact-checked research S10.)

citations.title: Dementia training for direct care staff
citations.requirement: Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S11.)

citations.title: Medication assistance training
citations.requirement: Homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+: 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S12.)

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: Care custodians and facility staff are mandated reporters. Report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then in writing within the statutory time (SOC 341). The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c). (Per fact-checked research S36.)

citations.title: Liability insurance minimums
citations.requirement: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence. (Per fact-checked research S18.)

citations.title: HCBS Settings Rule (applies to Assisted Living Waiver settings)
citations.requirement: HCBS settings must include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors. Applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver. (Per fact-checked research.)

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Annual fee of $495.60 (4–6 beds) or $742.80 (7–15 beds), due each license anniversary, with a 50% late fee. Capacity change fee of $25. (Per fact-checked research S1.)

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: At least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year. (Per fact-checked research S57.)

citations.title: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly
citations.requirement: Special meal and rest period rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel. (Per fact-checked research S60.)

citations.cite: LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B
citations.title: Application attachments (theft and loss policy B14; neighborhood complaint policy B15; sample menu B10; job descriptions B4–B5)
citations.requirement: Written theft and loss policy (B14); neighborhood complaint policy when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer (B15); sample menu (B10); job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5). (Per fact-checked research S21.)

citations.title: Workers' compensation coverage
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation insurance is required once the facility has employees; RCFEs are WCIRB class 9070(1). Cited in the fact-checked checklist; the section text was not fetched here and the URL is a code-index link only.

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: License Application and Applicant Forms (LIC 200, 215, 308, 309)
state_specifics: LIC 200: original signatures only. Every applicant signs, including each general partner. A corporation or LLC attaches a Board resolution authorizing the signers.
LIC 215: one per applicant, with current reference statements that are not from relatives.
LIC 308: name at least one person to act in the licensee's absence. The licensee cannot designate self. An entity attaches a resolution.
LIC 309: required only for a corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC. It must match the LIC 200.
Non-refundable application fee: $990 (4-6 beds) or $1,486.80 (7-15 beds), payable to CDSS. Mail the packet to the Centralized Applications Bureau, 744 P Street, MS 9-14-8201, Sacramento, CA 95814.

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Resident Cash Resources Affidavit and Surety Bond (LIC 400, LIC 402)
state_specifics: LIC 400: check the correct box and obtain a bond if the facility will hold resident cash.
LIC 402: use the LIC 402 language, name the State of California as beneficiary, show effective and expiration dates, and carry original seals and signatures.
The bond amount must match the amount on the LIC 400.
If the facility holds resident money, keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as residents' money (no commingling).

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Financial Forms and Start-Up Funds Verification (LIC 401, 401a, 403, 403a, 404)
state_specifics: LIC 401: resident count matches requested capacity, salaries are at least minimum wage, about 25% is added for fringe benefits (or explain why not), and rent matches the lease. File a separate LIC 401 for each other licensed facility.
LIC 401a: Part I is completed by individual applicants and each general partner; Part II by all applicants.
Complete the LIC 403a first, then the LIC 403. Use realistic figures. Only cash and cash equivalents count toward the 3-month start-up funds (22 CCR §87155).

LIC 404: the financial institution sends verification directly to the licensing agency. One form per bank, all account holders sign, and the account is in the applicant's name. A readily accessible line of credit is acceptable.
Every financial form shows the preparer's name and original signatures. Do not spend start-up funds on renovation or repair.

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Personnel Report and Staff Forms (LIC 500, 501, 503, 508)
state_specifics: LIC 500: list every planned position with days and hours covering all hours of operation. Show unhired positions as 'to be hired' by title. Sign the reverse side if there are fingerprint-exempt personnel.
LIC 501: needed only for non-licensee directors/administrators who do not complete an LIC 215. Keep other staff forms on file at the facility.
LIC 503: one each for the applicant or designee and the administrator. It must be under 6 months old at application, signed and dated by a qualified medical professional, and show the TB result.
LIC 508: one each for the applicant or designee and the administrator.
Staff health screening is due within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence.

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Emergency Disaster Plan, Facility Sketch and Fire Inspection Forms (LIC 610E, LIC 999, LIC 9054)
state_specifics: LIC 610E (the RCFE version of LIC 610D) shows two relocation sites away from the facility with room for all residents. If the applicant does not yet occupy the property, get written authorization to use each site.
LIC 999: dimensions and use of all rooms, door and window exits keyed by number to the LIC 610E exit routes, rooms for non-ambulatory residents and staff, and all indoor and outdoor space.

LIC 999 outdoor sketch shows driveways, fences, storage, gardens, recreation areas, major equipment, pools and utility shut-offs. Multi-building sites need one sketch per building plus an overall sketch.
LIC 9054 fire inspection is required for RCFEs. Fire clearance is needed before licensure (22 CCR §87202). No fire-inspection fee may be charged for homes of 6 or fewer (HSC §1569.84).

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Legal Entity Documents and Authority to Act (Partnership, Corporation, LLC)
state_specifics: Partnership: a written agreement is not needed for spouses. Two unrelated individuals must provide one. All general partners are named on the license and sign. Describe each general partner's duties and whether each can act for the others. For a limited partnership, list the limited partners' names and addresses.

Corporation: Articles of Incorporation with state seal; a foreign corporation also needs a California Secretary of State Certificate of Qualification. Add the constitution and by-laws and a Board Resolution naming the authorized signer.
Corporation: list directors' and officers' names, titles, addresses and phones, and the name and address of each 10% shareholder.
LLC: Articles of Organization stamped by the Secretary of State (a foreign LLC also files stamped form LLC-5). Add the operating agreement.
LLC: list managers, managing members and non-managing members holding 10% or more. If the signer's authority is not in the operating agreement, add a written delegation.

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Administrator Qualifications and Certification Verification
state_specifics: LIC 281 B2 refers to a 40-hour program. Current HSC §1569.616 requires an 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 live hours) plus the state exam within 60 days. Follow the statute and confirm with the Administrator Certification Bureau, 916-653-9300.
Submit proof of program registration with the application. A Department-issued certificate from an approved vendor is required before licensure.
Administrator: age 21+, high school diploma or equivalent, good character. 16+ beds add education and experience requirements.
Education: transcripts from an accredited school when required. For foreign schools, provide class descriptions, a catalog, or a local college equivalency.

Experience: written references showing the capacity, duties and dates, or a signed administrator declaration explaining why none could be obtained. Experience verification is not needed for a 1-6 bed RCFE.

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Job Descriptions and Personnel Policies
state_specifics: Write a job description for every classification on the LIC 500. Each states duties, minimum qualifications (licenses, certificates, skills tied to licensing requirements), and supervision given and received.
Include an awake night-shift duty statement and an administrator job description (premises hours, designated substitute).
Personnel policies show shifts and hours that match all personnel reports and give 24-hour competent coverage.
Staff are told in writing they must report abuse to the licensing agency, law enforcement and the adult protective/ombudsman agency (W&I §15630).

Hiring practice: screen education and experience. Conditions of employment are fingerprint clearance, criminal conviction statement, TB clearance, physical exam/health questionnaire and child abuse index check. Pay at least the state minimum wage ($16.90 in 2026) or a higher local rate, and give at least 40 hours of paid sick leave (Labor Code §246).

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: In-Service Training Plan, First Aid Cards and Orientation Certificate
state_specifics: New-employee training plan: describe the training and who conducts it. Direct care staff need 40 hours initial (20 before working alone, 20 within 4 weeks) and 20 hours annually.
Ongoing training plan: list topics (including administrator CE), frequency and documentation. Annual training includes 8 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports/restricted conditions/hospice.
Medication assistance: 10 hours initial plus an exam for homes of 15 or fewer (6 hands-on before assisting); 8 hours annually.
Administrator CE: 40 hours every 2 years, including 8 hours dementia.

Submit first aid cards for the applicant and administrators (verified by CDSS) and the Component I orientation certificate with the application. The certificate expires 30 days after access, so download it.

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Program Description and Plan of Operation
state_specifics: Cover philosophy and goals, days and hours of operation, a daily activity schedule and a one-month activity calendar. Say who plans, conducts and assists with each.
Describe basic services (per LIC 604/604A) and the optional services listed in the admission agreement.

Medical emergencies: call 9-1-1 for imminent threats, notify the physician and person responsible, and follow the reporting policy. Medication assistance is limited to self-administered medications (22 CCR §87465).
State transportation arrangements and the community resources and consultants used.
Include a licensing-approved procedure for immediate response to incidents and complaints. A pamphlet is acceptable only if every element B7.1-B7.11 is in it.

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Admission Policies
state_specifics: Cover who is accepted (age range, compatibility), rates and refund policy, acceptance and retention limits, pre-admission appraisal, needs and services plan, medical assessment and the admission agreement.
B9.2 (intake for group homes) applies to group homes only. State in the manual that it is not applicable to an RCFE.
Criteria for placement appropriateness: interview, paperwork, and suitability against admission criteria before admission (22 CCR §87457).

Residents are told their personal rights (22 CCR §87468.1) and that those rights will not be violated. Also cover emergency information, sign-in/sign-out, immunization and physical exam/TB requirements.
Exclude prohibited conditions (22 CCR §87615): stage 3-4 pressure injuries, G-tubes, NG tubes, tracheostomies, serious infections, and total dependence in all ADLs.

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Control of Property, Water Analysis and Insurance Information
state_specifics: B11: name and address of the property owner, plus a lease or rental agreement (any length) that allows facility use. If the agreement precludes use as a facility, the license is denied or withdrawn.
B11: if the applicant owns the property, provide a property tax bill, deed or other document showing the street address.

B12: if water comes from a well or other private source, submit an on-site source inspection and a bacteriological analysis signed by a qualified agency. This is required at initial licensure regardless of capacity. Retest annually for capacity 7-15.
B13: state whether the facility is insured, the coverage type and the carrier. HSC §1569.605 requires liability insurance of $1M per occurrence / $3M aggregate.
Workers' compensation is required once the facility has employees (RCFE class 9070(1)).

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Neighborhood Complaint Policy
state_specifics: Required in the RCFE column of the Section B table. LIC 281 text applies it to non-resident-owner facilities of 6 or fewer.
State procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints.
State a time when the owner, licensee or designee will meet with neighbors, and publish the contact number.
Keep a complaint log with date, complainant, response and resolution.

policies.category: Final checklist ('Have you remembered the following')
policies.title: Application Packet Final Checklist and Submission Review
state_specifics: Orientation certificate(s) for the facility type are enclosed.
The LIC 200 is signed and dated by all applicants. Every form has an original signature and date.
The Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610E) and facility sketch (LIC 999, showing indoor/outdoor space and all exits) are complete.
All financial information (LIC 401/401a/403/403a/404) is complete and the application fee check is enclosed.
Keep a full copy. Expect 90-120 days. Respond quickly to analyst deficiency requests.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The licensee and governing body are accountable for the facility's operation and compliance (22 CCR §87205; text not retrieved, verify before publishing).
A certified administrator is on the premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent.
Notify CDSS within 30 days of a new administrator and within 15 working days of a change of chief corporate officer (22 CCR §87211).
Written plan of operation covering administrative organization is kept current (22 CCR §87208).

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: Post the license, resident rights, emergency exit plans and phone numbers, and the Ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 with the local ombudsman number.
Pay the annual fee by each license anniversary: $495.60 (4-6 beds) or $742.80 (7-15). Late payment adds 50%.
Notify CDSS before changing capacity ($25) or relocating (50% of the application fee).
Fire clearance is needed before licensure and separately before accepting nonambulatory or bedridden residents (22 CCR §87202).
ASCP contact: (916) 657-2592. Advertising and license-number display follow 22 CCR §87206 (text not retrieved).

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Quality Assurance
state_specifics: Review all policies at least annually (facility standard). The infection control plan must be reviewed annually, after an outbreak declaration, or when the licensing agency asks.
Run quarterly internal mock inspections of medication records, personnel files (training, health screening, clearances), appraisals and admission agreements.
Trend incident, injury and grievance reports and record corrective actions.
Control versions: each policy shows an effective date and revision history, and a staff acknowledgment is kept.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity (including Assisted Living Waiver)
state_specifics: Do not make false claims or statements to licensing or payers (22 CCR §87207; text not retrieved).

If enrolled in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver (ALW): follow the DHCS provider agreement and tier rates. The waiver does not pay room and board; the resident pays it (typically the SSI/SSP basic rate of $1,444.07/month in 2026).
The HCBS settings rule applies only to ALW participants: a lease or agreement, privacy, choice, and access to food and visitors.

The DHCS enrollment packet is notarized (DHCS 6204, 6207, 6208) with a $750 CY2026 application fee. ALW providers need licensed nursing on call or employed, and an Individual Response System if housing more than 6 participants.

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Personal Rights and Discipline)
state_specifics: Post and give residents the 18 personal rights of 22 CCR §87468.1: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation and abuse; leaving at any time and not being locked in; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care.

The facility cannot deny admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, or association based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. The Department cannot waive these protections.
Staff are trained on personal rights (22 CCR §87411(c)(3)(C) cross-references §87468).
Discipline statement: no corporal or unusual punishment of any resident. The detailed LIC 281 B8 discipline-policy content is for group homes and FFAs only.

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: The grievance procedure is in the admission agreement. Residents are told how to complain to CDSS Community Care Licensing and the ombudsman.
Ombudsmen and advocates may visit privately at reasonable hours without prior notice.
Post the Ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local ombudsman number. ASCP: (916) 657-2592.
Log each grievance, response and outcome. Never retaliate.

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Individual written agreement in 12-point plain-language type with titled sections, signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Give a copy immediately and post a copy or notice of availability.
State basic and additional services, rates and payment terms, refund conditions, and preadmission fee limits and refunds.
Give 60 days' written notice of rate changes.
Include visiting and firearms policies, the grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights (wording from 22 CCR §87224, not modified), and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman.
Attach LIC 9158 when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Property and Theft and Loss
state_specifics: Residents keep and spend their own money (22 CCR §87468.1). Decide whether the facility holds cash; if yes, file LIC 400/402.
Held cash: receipts, accounting records, and a separate account titled as residents' money, never commingled.

Theft and loss policy (B14): inventory of personal property at admission, modification of the inventory, safeguarding property on death, documentation and reporting of loss, method of marking, and a secure safekeeping area.
Keep the inventory in the resident record and give the resident a copy.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Resuscitation Requests
state_specifics: Honor advance directives and resuscitative-measure requests per 22 CCR §87469 (text not retrieved; verify before publishing).
Staff call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health except where §87469(c)(2)-(4) applies (cross-referenced in §87465(g)).
Keep the directive or request in the resident record and make it available to staff and emergency responders.
Residents may refuse care (22 CCR §87468.1).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Residents have privacy in phone, mail and visits (22 CCR §87468.1). Privacy is also an HCBS setting requirement for ALW participants.

HIPAA applies if the facility is a covered entity (for example it conducts standard electronic transactions, as in ALW billing). Designate a privacy officer and issue a Notice of Privacy Practices if so.
Release resident information only with consent or as the law permits, including to licensing, the ombudsman and emergency responders.
Secure paper and electronic records. Report breaches to the administrator.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: No discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status in admission, transfer, discharge, room assignment or pronoun use (22 CCR §87468.1(b), not waivable).
Provide reasonable accommodation for disabilities, including LIC 9158 for hearing or other disabilities.
Provide interpreters or translated documents for residents with limited English proficiency.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Appraisal and Reassessment
state_specifics: Before admission, complete a pre-admission appraisal: interview, functional, mental and social evaluation, consent, and a suitability determination against admission criteria (22 CCR §87457).
Obtain a physician medical assessment and record functional capabilities, mental condition and social factors (22 CCR §§87458-87462; text not retrieved).
Reappraise per §87463 and when staff observe a change. Reappraisal also drives awake night supervision for residents with dementia (22 CCR §87705).
Screen for prohibited conditions (22 CCR §87615) before accepting any resident.

policies.title: Needs and Services Plan
state_specifics: Use the California term 'needs and services plan'. Base it on the appraisal.
Provide the basic services (22 CCR §87464; list in LIC 604/604A) and any additional services in the admission agreement.
Involve the resident and representative in decisions (22 CCR §87467). Staff observe the resident and note changes (§87466).
Update the plan at each reappraisal or change in condition.

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Cannot admit or retain residents who need health services for, or have: stage 3-4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, or tracheostomies (the list is not exhaustive).
Allowable and restricted health conditions and exceptions follow 22 CCR §§87609-87617 (text not retrieved).
Get a separate fire clearance before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents.
Hospice residents are served under an approved hospice care waiver (22 CCR §87632).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Eviction grounds and procedures follow 22 CCR §87224 and may not be modified (§87507(g)(10)); full text not retrieved.
The admission agreement states eviction grounds and notice rights and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman.
Department-ordered relocation follows §87223. Health-condition relocation orders and resident review requests follow §§87637-87639.
Residents may move out at any time (22 CCR §87468.1). No transfer or discharge on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity, expression or HIV status.

policies.title: Medication Management, Assistance, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Staff assist only with self-administered medications and give no injections unless authorized by law. Never force, hide or camouflage medications.
PRN orders: signed and dated physician order on a prescription blank stating symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours.
Central storage in a locked place, in the original container. Keep the medication record at least 1 year.
Destruction is done by the administrator and one other non-resident adult. Keep the record at least 3 years.
Medication-assist staff: 10 hours initial training (6 hands-on before assisting) plus an exam for homes of 15 or fewer; 8 hours annually.

policies.title: Incidental Medical Care, Nursing Oversight and Delegation
state_specifics: Maintain a plan for incidental medical and dental care (22 CCR §87465). RCFE staff do not perform services outside allowable health conditions.
Healing wounds and care of bedridden residents follow 22 CCR §§87631 and 87606 (text not retrieved; verify before publishing).
ALW providers need licensed nursing on call or employed.
Keep a first aid kit, post emergency numbers and keep an ambulance number available.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Call 9-1-1 for any imminent threat to health.

Notify the physician and the person responsible for the resident. Send a written report to CDSS and the responsible person within 7 days of a death, a serious injury as determined by the physician, or an incident threatening health or safety.
Reappraise after any change of condition and recheck against prohibited conditions (22 CCR §87615).
Outbreaks, poisonings and major accidents: report to licensing and the local health officer within 24 hours.

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: In homes under 16 beds, at least one night staff person is awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision (per appraisal, reappraisal or observation).

A facility advertising dementia care must have a written dementia program (philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition, success indicators). Keep advertisements for 3 years.
Direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annual dementia training (HSC §§1569.625, 1569.626).
Administrator CE includes 8 hours dementia.

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Stage 3-4 pressure injuries cannot be admitted or retained (22 CCR §87615).
Assess fall and skin risk at appraisal and reappraisal, and record it in the needs and services plan.
Physical plant: grab bars at toilets, tubs and showers, non-slip surfaces and emergency lighting (22 CCR §87303).
Postural supports follow 22 CCR §87608; staff get 4 hours of training on postural supports/restricted conditions/hospice.

policies.title: Hospice, Home Health Coordination and Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Hospice waiver: written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents. CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request (22 CCR §87632). Hospice care also follows §87633.
Notify the resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation (22 CCR §87212).
Report a death in writing to licensing and the person responsible within 7 days.
On death, safeguard personal property under the theft and loss policy and inventory it.
Coordinate home health and hospice care plans with the needs and services plan.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Staff are mandated reporters under W&I Code §15630. Use W&I §15630, not the Lanterman Act.

Report suspected physical abuse to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours (22 CCR §87211(b),(c)). Follow with the written SOC 341.
Ombudsman CRISISline: 1-800-231-4024. Residents are free from abuse, humiliation and intimidation (22 CCR §87468.1).
Protect residents from further harm, preserve evidence and never retaliate.

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Written report to licensing and the responsible person within 7 days of any death, physician-determined serious injury, AED use, or incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse).
Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: phone or fax to licensing and the local health officer within 24 hours.
Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority and by the next working day to licensing.
Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off notice. Civil penalty is $100 per day up to $2,000.

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Residents may leave at any time and cannot be locked in (22 CCR §87468.1).
Identify residents at risk of wandering at appraisal and provide awake night supervision when a resident with dementia needs it.
Search immediately, call law enforcement and notify the responsible person. Report an unexplained absence in writing within 7 days (22 CCR §87211).
Night staff must know the emergency plan.

policies.title: Restraints, Postural Supports and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Residents are free from punishment, humiliation and intimidation, may refuse care and cannot be locked in (22 CCR §87468.1).
Postural supports follow 22 CCR §87608 (text not retrieved). Staff get 4 hours of postural supports/restricted conditions/hospice training before working alone and annually.
Never force, hide or camouflage medications (chemical restraint prohibited in practice).
Document and review any restrictive intervention with the physician and responsible person.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Keep a written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan (LIC 610E) with staff assignments, fire safety plan, exits, assembly site, transportation and relocation sites equipped for temporary stay.
Cover supervision during evacuation, contact after relocation, contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies, and hospice notification.
Post emergency exit plans and telephone numbers.
Night staff know the emergency plan and are first-aid trained (22 CCR §87415).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Fire clearance is required before licensure and separately for nonambulatory or bedridden residents.
Fire safety, drills and extinguisher requirements follow 22 CCR §87203 (text not retrieved; confirm drill frequency before publishing).
Keep exit routes clear, emergency lighting working and exit plans posted.
No fire-inspection fee may be charged for homes of 6 or fewer (HSC §1569.84).
Keep fire drill logs on file.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282) naming an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional.
Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review the plan annually, after an outbreak declaration, or when licensing asks.
Staff TB screening: chest x-ray or intradermal test within 6 months before or 7 days after employment.
Report outbreaks within 24 hours to licensing and the local health officer.

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: State the visiting policy in the plan of operation and admission agreement.
State the firearms policy in the admission agreement.
Ombudsmen and advocates may visit privately without prior notice.
ALW participants have access to visitors under the HCBS settings rule.
Smoking and pet rules are facility policy; keep them consistent with fire safety and infection control.

policies.title: Food Service, Therapeutic Diets and Sample Menu
state_specifics: Sample menu (B10): one week of planned meals and snacks using the four basic food groups, with portion sizes and meal times.
Food service requirements are in 22 CCR Div. 6, Ch. 8, Art. 10 (section numbers not retrieved; pull the text before finalizing storage and therapeutic diet content).
Therapeutic diets only on a physician's order.
ALW participants have access to food under the HCBS settings rule.

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Planned activities follow 22 CCR §87219 (text not retrieved). Keep a daily schedule and a monthly calendar stating who plans and conducts each.
Resident councils follow 22 CCR §87221 (text not retrieved).
A facility advertising dementia care includes activities in its written dementia program.
Tailor activities to appraisals and the needs and services plan.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Heat at least 68°F; hot water 105-120°F (22 CCR §87303).
No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family (22 CCR §87307).
Keep the plant clean and in good repair, with grab bars, non-slip surfaces and emergency lighting.
Test any private water supply (annually for capacity 7-15).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: State transportation arrangements in the plan of operation.
Any charge for transportation is listed as an additional service with its rate in the admission agreement.
Drivers are staff and need criminal record clearance and training (facility practice).
Residents' rights to leave and to participate in community activities are preserved.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Night Supervision and Scheduling
state_specifics: No numeric ratio. Staff must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need (22 CCR §87411).
Night (10 p.m.-6 a.m.), under 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises. 16-100 residents: one awake employee plus one on call within 10 minutes.
Awake night staff are required in homes under 16 beds when a resident with dementia needs it.
Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers are supervised and not counted.
Wage Order 5 has special meal and rest rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Get employment counsel for live-in or 24-hour shifts.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, exemption or transfer is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and all staff before they work or are present.
Each person completes the criminal record statement (LIC 508).
Do not allow anyone without clearance, exemption or transfer to be present or work alone.
Keep clearance records in the personnel file.

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Direct care staff: 40 hours initial (20 before working alone, including 6 dementia and 4 postural supports/restricted conditions/hospice; the second 20, including 6 dementia, within 4 weeks); 20 hours annually (8 dementia).
Medication assistance (15 or fewer beds): 10 hours (6 hands-on first, 4 within 2 weeks) plus exam; 8 hours annually. 16+ beds: 24 hours (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus exam.
First aid from a qualified provider for care staff.
Administrator: 80-hour program, exam, then 40 hours CE every 2 years including 8 dementia.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: All personnel need a physician health screening, including a chest x-ray or intradermal TB test, within 6 months before or 7 days after employment (22 CCR §87411(f)).
Complete LIC 503 for staff.
Exposure control follows the infection control plan and OSHA bloodborne pathogen rules.
Keep results in the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep a personnel file for each employee (22 CCR §87412; text not retrieved).
Include training documentation, sign-in sheets, health screening (LIC 503), criminal record statement (LIC 508), clearance proof, first aid card and personnel record (LIC 501).
Training documentation is stored in the personnel record (§87411(c)(6) cross-reference).
Keep job descriptions and supervision lines on file.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff protect residents' dignity and freedom from humiliation and intimidation, and use residents' preferred names and pronouns (22 CCR §87468.1).
Staff do not handle resident cash or accept gifts except under the resident funds policy and safeguards (facility practice).
Staff report suspected abuse as mandated reporters.
Violations lead to discipline up to termination.

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Maintain resident records and a register of residents (22 CCR §§87506, 87508; content and retention periods not retrieved. Do not state a general retention period until §87506 is read).
Keep the admission agreement, appraisal, medical assessment, needs and services plan, advance directive and property inventory in the record.
Medication records at least 1 year; destruction records at least 3 years (22 CCR §87465).
Keep dementia advertisements for 3 years.
If HIPAA applies, follow 45 CFR 164.530 administrative requirements.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: 7-day written reports for deaths, serious injuries, AED use and threatening incidents. 24-hour reports for outbreaks and poisonings. Report fires immediately and to licensing by the next working day.
Abuse: 2 hours (serious bodily injury) or 24 hours, then SOC 341.

Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off. Notify within 30 days of a new administrator and within 15 working days of a change of chief corporate officer.
Annual license fee on each anniversary; $25 for a capacity change.
Administrator certificate renewal every 2 years (40 hours CE; $140 renewal fee).

documents.title: Application Instructions for A Facility License (Section A forms; Section B supportive documents / plan of operation items)
documents.issuer: California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD)
documents.version: The CDSS Forms I-L page lists LIC 281 (11/25) as the current edition. I could not open that PDF because cdss.ca.gov returned a permission error for the Portals URL. The item list below comes from the full LIC 281 (9/04) text, retrieved from the cdss.ca.gov /cdssweb/entres/forms/english/lic281.pdf URL. It matches the owner-supplied text. Compare it against the 11/25 PDF before submitting.
documents.url: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Portals/9/Additional-Resources/Forms-and-Brochures/2020/I-L/LIC281.pdf?ver=cDy_GGClLQ7_6gtjxO-jNQ%3d%3d (current per CDSS forms list; 9/04 text read at https://www.cdss.ca.gov/cdssweb/entres/forms/english/lic281.pdf)
documents.how_used: The reviewer uses LIC 281 as the packet checklist. Section A lists the LIC forms. Section B lists the plan-of-operation documents and policies. Item numbers below are the document's own (A1-A16, B1-B17). The document uses bullets inside each B item, so sub-items are numbered here in bullet order (e.g., B7.1). Items for other facility types (A9.A, A17, B3, B18) are omitted.

required_items.text: LIC 200 - Application for a Community Care Facility or Residential Care Facility for the Elderly License. Form filled out completely; all applicants sign, including each general partner; original signatures only (no photocopied signatures); signatures match the applicant's name unless the applicant is a corporation or LLC; if a corporation applies, the Board resolution authorizing the signers must be submitted with the form.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A1 p.3

required_items.text: LIC 215 - Applicant Information. One form completed by each applicant; original signatures; reference statements must be current and should not be from relatives.

LIC 308 - Designation of Facility (Administrative) Responsibility. At least one individual must be designated to act in the licensee's absence; a licensee cannot designate himself or herself; a corporation or LLC must submit a resolution authorizing the delegation; original signatures.

LIC 309 - Administrative Organization. Not required of individual applicants; required if the applicant is a corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC; information must match the LIC 200; terms of office should match articles/bylaws.
LIC 400 - Affidavit Regarding Client Cash Resources. Form completed with the appropriate box checked; make sure a bond is obtained if needed; original signatures.

LIC 402 - Surety Bond. Must use the LIC 402 language; State of California identified as beneficiary; effective and expiration dates; original seals and signatures; bond amount must match the amount on the LIC 400.

LIC 401 - Monthly Operating Statement. Number of clients corresponds to requested capacity; other facility income clear and documented; operating costs indicated and reasonable (salaries at least minimum wage); approximately 25 percent of salaries added for fringe benefits (or explain why not); rent matches lease/rental/mortgage payment; separate LIC 401 for each other licensed facility; indicate estimated or actual; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 401a - Supplemental Financial Information. Part I (other income and expenses, excluding facility income) completed by individual applicants and each general partner; Part II completed by all applicants; preparer name and original signature.

LIC 403 - Balance Sheet. Complete the LIC 403a first; reflect assets and liabilities of all owner activities; figures must be 'realistic'; life insurance at cash/surrender value; real estate shown per applicant type; on-site furnishings and equipment at market value; only cash and cash equivalents count toward the three-month start-up funds; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 403a - Balance Sheet Supplemental Schedule. Detailed balance sheet completed before the LIC 403; cash in the bank verified with the LIC 404; liabilities verified by credit report; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 404 - Financial Information Release and Verification. Used to verify approximately three months of operating funds; a verifiable line of credit is acceptable if readily accessible; start-up funds should not be consumed on renovation or repair; the financial institution must send the verification directly to the licensing agency (the licensee cannot hand-carry it); one form or set per bank; all persons on an account sign; accounts in the applicant's name; original signatures.

LIC 500 - Personnel Report. Show all planned employee positions, with days and hours of duty (reviewed for required staff coverage for all hours of operation); list the Director/Administrator and any staff already hired; list unhired positions as 'to be hired' by position title; reverse side signed if there are fingerprint-exempt personnel; separate LIC 500 for each other licensed facility; original signatures.

LIC 501 - Personnel Record. Only for those who do not complete an LIC 215; submitted with the application only for directors/administrators who are not licensees; other staff forms are kept on file at the facility.

LIC 503 - Health Screening Report - Facility Personnel. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator; for RCFE applicants the screening must be less than six months old at the time of application; must be signed and dated by a qualified medical professional (no photocopied signatures); TB test portion completed including result, or separate test verification attached.
LIC 508 - Criminal Record Statement. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A13 p.9

required_items.text: LIC 610D (RCFE only: LIC 610E) - Emergency Disaster Plan. The plan must show two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate the number of residents; if the applicant does not currently occupy the property, use of the relocation site requires authorization from the agency or person in possession, verified in writing.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A14 p.9

required_items.text: LIC 999 - Facility Sketch. Dimensions and use of all rooms; door and window exits shown, with exit routes indicated by number as on the LIC 610 Emergency Disaster Plan; rooms for non-ambulatory residents and staff identified; sketch of all indoor and outdoor space (driveways, fences, storage, gardens, recreation areas); separate sketches per building plus one overall sketch for multi-building sites; outdoor sketch shows dimensions, location of major equipment and swimming pools, and utility shut-off locations.
LIC 9054 - Fire Inspection. Listed as 'Required' for RCFE in the Section A table; no further instruction text appears for A16 in LIC 281.
Partnership Agreement / Articles of Incorporation / Articles of Organization. Required for RCFE; it tells the licensing agency who is ultimately responsible for which functions in the facility.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B1 p.11

required_items.text: Partnership: a written agreement is not necessary when partners are husband and wife; two individuals not related by marriage must provide a partnership agreement.

Partnership: determine whether it is a general or limited partnership; for a limited partnership only the general partner(s) are on the license, but names and addresses of limited partners are also needed.
Partnership: all general partners need to be on the license and sign the application; name and business address of each general partner is needed.
Partnership: a description of the obligations and duties of each general partner and whether or not each can act on behalf of the others.

Articles of Incorporation: establish the applicant is a valid corporation qualified to do business in California; a seal from the state of incorporation should be attached; foreign (out-of-state) corporations must also provide a Certificate of Qualification from the California Secretary of State.
Corporation: constitution and by-laws (day-to-day operation).
Corporation: Board Resolution identifying the agents acting for the corporation, including authorization to apply for a license and the person authorized to sign and act on its behalf.
Corporation: directors' and officers' names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers; name and address of 10 percent shareholders.
Articles of Organization (LLC): stamped by the Secretary of State; a foreign LLC must also submit Secretary of State Form LLC-5 stamped by the California Secretary of State.

LLC: operating agreement; names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers of all managing members, managers, and non-managing members holding a 10 percent or more interest. If the signer is not identified in the operating agreement as having authority, a written delegation of authority consistent with the operating agreement is necessary.

Verification of Administrator Qualifications - For RCFE only: proof of registration in a 40-hour certification program submitted with the application; a Department-issued certificate verifying completion of the 40-hour RCFE certification program by an approved vendor is required prior to licensure.
Education: transcripts from an accredited school, when required; for out-of-country schools, class descriptions or college catalog, or certification of class equivalency from a local college.

Experience: written references obtained by the applicant/licensee and submitted (showing the person worked there, in what capacity, specific duties, and for what period); if references cannot be obtained, a declaration signed by the Administrator stating why and the same details.
Verification of experience for an applicant applying for a one to six bed ARF or RCFE is not necessary.

Job Descriptions - a job description for each staff classification; there must be a job description for each classification listed on the LIC 500, and staff positions must correspond to those listed on all personnel reports.
Each job description must address: duties and responsibilities.
Each job description must address: minimum qualifications that correspond to licensing requirements, including any special licenses, certificates or special skills needed for the job.
Each job description must address: lines of supervision (supervision given and to whom, and supervision received and from whom).
Personnel Policies - work hours/shifts documenting positions that provide coverage with competent staff, corresponding with the positions, work days and hours on all personnel reports.

Personnel Policies - abuse reporting procedures; documentation must indicate employees will be informed of their responsibilities to report to the licensing agency as well as to the police and child/adult protective agency.

Personnel Policies - hiring practices, including screening for necessary education and experience, and informing employees that conditions of employment include fingerprint clearance, statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, physical examination/health questionnaire, and child abuse index check.

In-Service Training for Staff - a plan for in-service training submitted at the time of application, as part of the plan of operation. New employee training: a description of the training and who will conduct it.

Ongoing training: topics to be covered (the list should include administrator continuing education units); how often the training will be given; how the training will be documented; must include topics specified in the regulation sections listed (for RCFE: 87565 Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly Regulations; 80065 General Regulations also listed).
Program Description (CCF/RCFE) - brief statement of the purpose, goals and program methods (program philosophy). A pamphlet or brochure is acceptable if all of the elements B7.1-B7.11 are included.
Days and hours of operation.
Daily schedule of activities provided by the facility, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
A one month schedule of planned social, educational and recreational activities, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
Description of the basic services provided by the facility (see Admission Guideline LIC 604 or 604A for a list of basic services).
Description of the optional services provided in the facility as listed in the admission agreement.
Description of how the facility will handle medical emergencies if a client becomes ill or injured.
Procedure for handling and assisting clients/residents with self-administered medications.
Transportation arrangements.
Description of community resources and consultants to be used by the facility.
A procedure (approved by the licensing agency) for immediate response to incidents and complaints.

Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights (titled 'Discipline Policies' in the text) - personal rights applies to all facility categories. The detailed discipline-policy content in the document is for group homes and foster family agencies only.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B8 p.17

required_items.text: The Department evaluates the discipline policies to ensure they do not violate personal rights and that there is a clear statement that no corporal or unusual punishment will be used; further information may be requested if the statements are unclear.

Admission Policies - persons accepted for care, including age range and compatibility determination process, when necessary. Overall, the policies must provide ages of clients, rates and refund policies, acceptance and retention limitations, pre-admission appraisals, needs and services plans, medical assessments, and an admission agreement.
Intake procedures for placement in group homes (listed in the document's B9 list; it names group homes only).
Criteria for assessing appropriateness of placement given an individual client's needs (interviews, procedures for obtaining and developing the necessary paperwork, etc.).
Needs and services plan.
Client's Rights/Personal Rights (at a minimum a statement that residents will be informed of their rights and that their rights will not be violated).
Medical assessment.
Pre-admission appraisal plan.
Emergency information.
Sign-in and sign-out procedures.
Immunization requirements.
Physical examination requirements (including TB testing).
Sample Menu - planned meals and snacks for one week, with foods from the four basic food groups.
Sample Menu - portion sizes.
Sample Menu - times meals served.
Control of Property - name and address of the owner of the property.

Control of Property - a copy of the lease or rental agreement (no requirement on length). If the agreement precludes use as a facility or operation is contrary to its terms, the license must be denied/withdrawn.
Control of Property - proof of ownership if the applicant owns the property (property tax bill, deed or other document containing the facility street address).

Bacterial Analysis of Water - only if the facility gets water from a well or other private source (required at initial licensure regardless of number of clients): evidence of on-site inspection of the source and a bacteriological analysis by a local or state health department or other qualified laboratory establishing the water is safe; analysis signed by a qualified agency representative.

Insurance Information (RCFE only) - a statement on whether there will be insurance covering the facility operation; if so, the type of coverage and with whom; if none, a statement of such is sufficient.

Theft and Loss Policy (RCFE only) - must include provisions for inventory of personal property at admission, modification of the inventory, practices to safeguard personal property upon the death of the resident, documentation and reporting of loss of personal property, method of marking personal property, and method for providing a secure area for safekeeping of resident personal property.

Neighborhood Complaint Policy - procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints, including a time when the owner, licensee or designee will be available to meet with neighborhood residents. The text says it is applicable to non-resident owner community care facilities providing care for six or fewer persons only; the Section B table marks it 'Required' in the RCFE column.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B15 p.20

required_items.text: First Aid Card - staff providing direct care and supervision must receive first aid training from qualified persons (e.g., American Red Cross); copies of first aid cards for applicant/administrators must be submitted and will be verified.
Orientation Certificate - proof of attendance must be submitted with the application.
Final checklist: Have you attended an orientation for your facility type and submitted a copy of your orientation certificate(s)?
Final checklist: Is your application (LIC 200) signed and dated by all applicants?
Final checklist: Do you have an Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610)?
Final checklist: Do you have a Facility Sketch (LIC 999) showing indoor/outdoor space as well as all exits?
Final checklist: Have you completed all Financial Information to operate your facility?
Final checklist: Have you enclosed your application fee?
Final checklist: Be sure all necessary information is completed, properly signed (original signature) and dated.

sections: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
Final checklist ('Have you remembered the following')

official.notes: LIC 281 has no single 'plan of operation' form. The application fee plus Section A and Section B documents go to the licensing agency as one packet. Per LIC 281, submit them in the same sequence as the booklet. An incomplete packet is returned in full. All forms need original signatures and dates, and the applicant should keep a photocopy. The reviewer compares documents against each other: job descriptions (B4) must match the LIC 500; work hours in the personnel policies (B5) must match the personnel reports; and the exit routes on the LIC 999 must match the LIC 610 plan. Organize the manual by B-number in this order: B1, B2, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 (only if the water supply is private), B13, B14, B15, B16, B17. B15 (neighborhood complaint policy) is marked 'Required' for RCFE in the table, but the B15 text limits it to non-resident-owner facilities of six or fewer. B9 includes a group-home intake bullet, and B8's discipline detail is for group homes and FFAs only. B7 says its '**' items may also appear in 'Section B10 - Admission Policies'; the document most likely means B9. Newer program-specific plan-of-operation content, such as the infection control plan and the dementia and hospice waivers listed in your regulations, is not in LIC 281. Use the Title 22 sections you listed (87208 plan of operation and others) as supplements. The CDSS forms page lists the current edition as LIC 281 (11/25), which I could not retrieve, so confirm the numbering against it before filing.
